home.about_p1: It started out under the name "Sorakaze," adding three mods — guns, rail, and building materials — on top of an otherwise vanilla survival experience. From there it kept expanding with craftable items, and was renamed "Glimpse Alpha" in v1.8.0. It's now a {mod_count}-mod pack that includes bosses, a new dimension, survival features, vehicles, and power infrastructure.
home.about_p2: The consistent policy has been to never replace or remove vanilla content — things like bows and minecarts remain exactly as they were. No real-world firearm, company, or trademark names are used.

changelog.title: Missile launcher targeting redesigned: click a tactical map instead of typing coordinates
changelog.summary: Missile launcher targeting has been redesigned from typed coordinates to a point-and-click tactical map. The map shows a range ring (2,000 blocks by default), and the selected point is colour-coded to show at a glance whether it's in range. The actual impact height is now determined automatically from the real ground surface at the selected point, computed by the server. Selecting an area that hasn't been loaded yet fails with a clear message instead of failing silently. Range checking now uses horizontal distance only, so terrain height differences can no longer make the map's range ring disagree with what the launcher will actually accept. Existing safety, firing, warhead, and cooldown systems are unchanged. The launcher's in-world 3D model has not been changed in this update.
highlights: Added an "Open Map" button to the missile launcher's control panel; the typed-coordinate fields have been removed.

Tactical map: shows the launcher centred, a range ring (2,000 blocks by default), your own position, and the selected pin. The pin is colour-coded (in range / out of range) with the distance shown as text.

Confirming sends only the selected XZ point to the server, which determines the real impact height from the ground surface itself. Confirming a point in an area that isn't loaded shows a clear "area not loaded" message and leaves the existing target unchanged.
Range checking changed from full 3D distance to horizontal distance only, so terrain height differences can no longer make the map's range ring and the actual firing gate disagree.
known_limitations: The launcher's in-world 3D model (its appearance) has not been changed in this update - it keeps its existing look.
The map does not support zooming or panning yet - it always shows a fixed-scale view centred on the launcher.

The ground-height preview under the pin only works for areas already loaded on your own client, which is most of the time outside view distance for a 2,000-block range - it will usually show "unknown until confirmed" (the server always computes the real height correctly once you confirm).

changelog.title: Admin app login consolidated to a single shared credential; fixed operator permissions being wiped
changelog.summary: Reports of "I enter the admin ID and password and still can't log in" persisted, so the owner decided to redesign the admin app's sign-in model itself. It no longer binds 3 separate accounts to 3 specific Minecraft names - there is now a single shared ID and password, and anyone who knows both can sign in from any Minecraft account. While investigating, a serious separate bug was found: when the admin account file is missing or broken, the server would automatically strip real operator (/op) permission from every player who had it - introduced in V2.4.0, this had been silently blocking command usage and things like the auto-backup toggle. That is also fixed in this release.
highlights: Admin app sign-in changed from 3 name-locked accounts to a single shared ID and password. Anyone who knows both can sign in, regardless of which Minecraft account they're connected as.

Fixed a serious bug where the automatic server-operator (/op) sync would strip operator permission from every existing operator whenever the admin account file was missing or broken. It now leaves existing operator status untouched until the file is properly configured.
For server owners: updated the credential-recovery steps for the new single-account model (private documentation).
warnings: Admin app access is now a single shared credential rather than per-person. To revoke access from one specific person without affecting everyone else is no longer possible with this design - rotate the shared password instead and redistribute it only to who should keep access.

changelog.title: Server Admin login now distinguishes the real cause, plus 3 known issues fixed
changelog.summary: A fix release for reports of "I enter the admin ID and password and still can't log in." No defect was found in the network path or the credential-verification logic itself, but the sign-in screen previously showed the exact same "wrong ID or password" message whether the server simply had zero admin accounts configured yet, or the entered credentials were genuinely wrong - there was no way to tell which. It now shows a distinct message for the former case, and login attempts made in that state no longer count against the anti-brute-force limiter. Also fixes 3 items that had been sitting on the Wiki's Known Issues page: reinforced glass window colour names, a cable glow bug right after a power off/on toggle, and the "Lookup" app's recipe grid layout.
highlights: Server Admin app sign-in screen: when the server has zero valid admin accounts configured, it now shows a clear message saying so instead of the generic "wrong ID or password". Login attempts made in this state are no longer counted toward the anti-brute-force lockout.
Fixed the reinforced glass window (17 colours) display names - every colour now shows its proper Japanese/English name.
Fixed cables that were disconnected from a breaker panel sometimes staying lit right after switching the main breaker off and back on.
Fixed the "Lookup" app's 3x3 recipe grid to show ingredients in their real crafting-grid positions (including empty cells), instead of packing them in order from the top-left.
For server owners: clarified the check/recovery steps for when a missing or malformed admin_account.json turns out to be the actual login cause (private owner-facing documentation).
known_limitations: The admin login fix addresses the "zero accounts configured" case specifically. If all 3 accounts are correctly configured but one specific account still can't sign in, that is a different symptom - please report it separately.

The orphaned-cable fix takes full effect from an update correctly applied on this version onward. If you jump straight from V2.4.2 or earlier, one already-orphaned cable may still show live once; breaking and replacing it, or the next breaker toggle, clears it.

changelog.title: Initial Release: 3 Mods — Guns, Rail, and Building Materials
changelog.summary: The server got its first three mods: "sorakaze_guns" (Guns), "sorakaze_rail" (Rail), and "sorakaze_deco" (Building Materials). Vanilla bows and minecarts are untouched — you can now craft new weapons, vehicles, and city-building blocks in survival.
highlights: Guns mod: the Assault Rifle, Shotgun, and Sniper Rifle, plus their dedicated ammo (rifle rounds, shotgun shells, sniper rounds), are now craftable
Added a scope zoom feature to the Sniper Rifle
Rail mod: added a new vehicle, the "Train," that you can place on rails (vanilla minecarts, rails, bows, and crossbows are unchanged). A looping running sound plays while it's moving

Building Materials mod: added 12 kinds of blocks, including guardrails, utility poles, power lines, tactile paving (directional/warning), vehicle traffic lights, pedestrian traffic lights, aircraft warning lights, and spotlights
warnings: Making the server mod-capable requires migrating from vanilla to Fabric. Also, running Minecraft 26.2 requires Java 25 or later, so please check the Java version on the server machine (see the admin install guide for setup steps)

changelog.title: Train Behavior Improvements & Gun Buffs
changelog.summary: Fixed the choppy train movement and the issue where you had to keep holding W just to keep moving. Buffed gun damage, and added a dedicated scope overlay and aim sway to the Sniper Rifle. The Building Materials mod also gained 4 new door types, including an automatic door.
highlights: Train: fixed choppy movement — it now runs smoothly
Train: pressing W once now locks in automatic acceleration and cruising with no further input needed (previously you had to hold it down). S brakes, and pressing S again after stopping reverses
Train top speed increased from 15 to 20 m/s. Reworked the train item's icon
Sniper Rifle: changed to an "aim, then release to fire" system, and added a dedicated scope overlay, ×4/×8 zoom (switch with scroll), and aim sway that's halved while sneaking
Assault Rifle: added increased spread while firing on the move

Building Materials mod: added 4 new door types — Automatic Door, Fusuma (sliding paper door), Large Door (iron/wood), and Hatch (multi-block structures that drop a single item no matter which part you break)
balance_changes: Assault Rifle: damage 3.0 → 5.0, fire rate 8 → 10 rounds/sec
Shotgun: pellet damage 2.0 → 3.0 (pellet count increased to 10), effective range 12 → 16m

changelog.title: Fixed Door Suffocation Bug & Major Train Speed Boost
changelog.summary: Fixed a serious bug where you could take damage just from walking through a door. Raised the train's top speed to 60 m/s (config cap 80 m/s), and it now automatically preloads chunks ahead in its direction of travel while running. Also added new blocks like the elevator and conveyor belt, and unified gun controls to left-click to fire, right-click to aim, and R to reload.
highlights: [Important] Fixed a bug where you'd take damage just from passing through a door (automatic doors, fusuma, large doors, hatches). Improved so doors won't auto-close while someone is nearby
Train top speed 20 → 60 m/s (config cap can be raised up to 80 m/s). It now auto-preloads chunks ahead of travel direction while moving, reducing scenery pop-in at high speed
4 new blocks: the Elevator (jump to go up / sneak to go down), Escalator, 2 kinds of chairs, and the Conveyor Belt (moves items, stoppable with redstone)
Overhauled gun controls: left-click to fire, hold right-click to aim (scope for the sniper), R to reload
Guns now render as 3D models when held (previously they were just the same flat icon as the GUI)
The shotgun can now one-shot an unarmored enemy at point-blank range (also fixed a bug where hit invincibility frames were nullifying multiple pellets at once)
balance_changes: Shotgun: pellet damage 3.0 → 5.0 (10 pellets; 50.0 total if every pellet lands at point-blank range)
Train: top speed 20 → 60 m/s, config cap 25 → 80 m/s
warnings: The meaning of the train's speed cap has changed, so after updating we recommend deleting config/sorakaze_rail.json (otherwise it'll stay at the old 20 m/s setting)

changelog.title: Guns Switched to Hitscan & Fixed Doors Not Staying Still
changelog.summary: Changed guns to a hitscan system where shots land the instant you fire, and added dedicated gunshot sounds. The train gained a 3D model and coupling (freight car, passenger car), and we fixed a bug where closed doors kept jittering. Hidden doors and 3 new door types make their debut too.
highlights: Changed guns to a hitscan system so shots land without waiting for a bullet to travel (hit-detection range: 60m for the Assault Rifle, 24m for the Shotgun, 150m for the Sniper Rifle)
Added new gunshot, reload, and dry-fire sounds (custom-made audio)
Enlarged guns when held, adjusted to look better in both first- and third-person
Added a 3D model to the train (commuter-train styling). You can now couple a Freight Car (27-slot storage) and Passenger Car (2 riders) to it (can't reverse while coupled)
Fixed closed doors continuously jittering
Added Hidden Doors (disguise themselves as dirt, stone, netherrack, end stone, and more)
Added 3 new door types (Roller Shutter, Sliding Door, Jail Bar Door), bringing the total to 9 door types

changelog.title: Boss & Vehicles Mods Debut — Now 5 Mods Total
changelog.summary: Two new mods, Boss and Vehicles, joined the lineup, bringing the total to 5 mods. Now featured: a boss fight where defeating a Warden in an Ancient City spawns the boss "Sculk Golem," 13 vehicle types including cars, trucks, and planes, and new items like the Laser Gun and laser traps. The train also now supports coupling up to 15 cars into one train.
highlights: New mod "Boss" debuts: defeating 3 Wardens in an Ancient City spawns the boss "Sculk Golem" (900 HP). Defeating it guarantees a drop of the "Enhanced Beacon," which has 3x the effect range

New mod "Vehicles" debuts: adds 10 land vehicle types (cars, buses, trucks, motorcycles, and more) plus 3 aircraft types. Includes features like rotating beacons and sirens on emergency vehicles and truck beds
Added the Laser Gun (1 Energy Cell = 100 shots) and Auto Turret (only targets hostiles) to the Guns mod
Added Laser Emitters/Receivers and tables to the Building Materials mod
Improved the train coupling system to support trains of up to 15 cars, including freight and passenger cars. Also added 2 bullet-train types with a 75 m/s lead car
known_limitations: Aircraft handling (takeoff, landing, stalling, etc.) is designed with future tuning in mind. If it feels heavy or hard to control, it can be adjusted via config

changelog.title: Fixed the Boss Getting Killed by Wardens
changelog.summary: Fixed a bug where the Sculk Golem — a precious boss limited to one per city and one per lifetime — could be killed by a retaliating Warden.
highlights: The Sculk Golem no longer takes damage from Wardens, and Wardens no longer attack or hunt Sculk Golems (players can still defeat it as before)

changelog.title: Vehicles Enlarged & New Nether Boss "Rock Lock"
changelog.summary: Scaled up cars, trains, and aircraft to be clearly bigger than the player, with more realistic proportions. Buffed the Assault Rifle and Laser Gun's damage 4x. A new boss, "Rock Lock," now appears in the Nether, and defeating it drops the powerful sword "Excalibur."
highlights: Enlarged cars, buses, trucks, motorcycles, trains, and aircraft (cars by about 1.6x, trains by 1.8x, large airliners by 2.2x, etc. — the scale varies by type)
The new boss "Rock Lock" now appears in the Nether. Summon it with a dedicated summoning item (craftable from 8 Nether Bricks + an Ender Eye), or use one that naturally spawns near Nether Fortresses
Defeating Rock Lock guarantees a drop of the sword "Excalibur" (high durability, fireproof, sets targets on fire on hit)
balance_changes: Assault Rifle: damage 5.0 → 20.0 (4x)
Laser Gun: damage 2.0 → 8.0 (4x)
warnings: You need to delete config/sorakaze_guns.json for the gun damage increase to take effect
Since vehicles and trains got bigger, be careful navigating narrow roads, tunnels, and hangars
known_limitations: How often Rock Lock's summoning item naturally spawns near Nether Fortresses hasn't been confirmed (the frequency can be adjusted via config)

changelog.title: Added 138 Building Blocks & Implemented Gun Durability
changelog.summary: A follow-up based on feedback after the v1.3.2 release. Reworked the appearance of 2 bosses, and fixed the gun durability bar, which had only ever been a display up to now, to finally actually decrease. The Building Materials mod gained 138 new building blocks, and every gun's range was extended 5x.
highlights: Reworked the appearance of the Sculk Golem and Rock Lock (Sculk Golem now looks like an Iron Golem made of sculk; Rock Lock now looks like a near-future armed robot). No changes to their strength or attacks

Fixed guns' durability to finally decrease properly (previously the durability bar just displayed without actually breaking). Default durability is now roughly 1,536 shots, and Excalibur's is roughly 6,093 hits
Extended every gun's range 5x (Assault Rifle 60 → 300m, Shotgun 24 → 120m, Sniper Rifle 150 → 750m, Laser Gun 80 → 400m)
Added 138 new building blocks to the Building Materials mod (vertical slabs, octagonal-pillar columns, and 8-step slopes, across 46 different materials)

Approved a plan to gradually redesign vehicles with "rounded, realistic shapes," and finished design mockups for the sedan and propeller plane (rolling this out across all 13 vehicle types is planned for future updates)
balance_changes: Extended every gun's range 5x (Assault Rifle 60 → 300m / Shotgun 24 → 120m / Sniper Rifle 150 → 750m / Laser Gun 80 → 400m)
warnings: You need to delete config/sorakaze_guns.json for the range extension to take effect
known_limitations: The "rounded design" for vehicles is currently just mockups for the sedan and propeller plane — rolling it out to all 13 types is planned for a future update

changelog.title: 5 New Bosses Arrive, Breaking the HP Ceiling
changelog.summary: Added 5 new colossal bosses to the Boss mod. We removed the vanilla Minecraft limitation that capped HP at 1024, so these are proper bosses with 2,400-4,000 HP. Defeating one guarantees a drop of a dedicated overpowered tool (pickaxe, axe, hoe, the new weapon "Spear," or shovel).
highlights: Added 5 new bosses, summoned with craftable summoning items: Runecore Colossus (3,000 HP), Emberlord (3,400 HP), Elder Treant (4,000 HP), Void Stalker (2,400 HP), and Frost Lich King (2,800 HP)

Defeating each boss guarantees a drop of a dedicated overpowered tool: Runecore Pickaxe, Ember Axe, Treant Hoe, Void Spear (a new weapon type vanilla doesn't have), and Frost Shovel. All have high durability and come pre-enchanted with multiple enchantments, and can't be crafted
known_limitations: All 5 are designed to be tough fights, expected to be a struggle solo. If they feel too strong, admins can adjust their HP and attack power via config
Void Stalker was designed to float in the air, but is currently implemented as moving on the ground plus teleporting

changelog.title: Complete Visual Overhaul for All 5 Bosses
changelog.summary: In response to feedback that they "looked like palette-swaps of the same creature," we completely reworked the appearance of all 5 new bosses. Gameplay — strength, drops, attacks, and so on — is unchanged.
highlights: Runecore Colossus: a stone core with bronze/gold armor plating, 2 swords floating at its sides, and rotating rune rings encircling its arms
Emberlord: lava veins running through its body, and 2 horns that curl upward in 4 jointed segments
Elder Treant: 8 branches, each angled and broken differently (3 of them snapped partway), and a face carved into its trunk
Void Stalker: abandoned its humanoid shape for a mass of obsidian, a purple portal, 8 tentacles, and 18 glowing eyes
Frost Lich King: a 5-tiered robe, a 9-spike jagged ice crown, and a rotating ice emblem hovering above its raised left hand

changelog.title: Boss Attack Animations & 3D Tool Models
changelog.summary: Added dedicated animations for each of the 5 bosses' melee, AoE, and beam attacks. The 5 tools they drop (pickaxe, axe, hoe, spear, shovel) were also reworked from flat icons into proper 3D models. Gameplay — damage, cooldowns, and so on — is unchanged.
highlights: Added dedicated animations for each of the 5 bosses' attacks (melee, 2 kinds of AoE, and beam), making attack telegraphs (windup motions) easier to read
Reworked the 5 droppable tools into proper 3D models. GUI icons now show the 3D render too
known_limitations: Melee attacks don't have a windup like a raised-arm animation. Since vanilla melee damage triggers instantly, adding a windup would throw off the timing of when damage actually lands

changelog.title: Sky Dimension Arrives, Bosses Get Signature Moves
changelog.summary: Added a new dimension, "Sky," reachable through portals that rarely generate on the overworld surface. You can now trade with Angel Merchants and equip glider gear. All 10 bosses now have signature moves, and can be summoned anytime with a summoning stone. Building Materials crafting also gained selectable recipe buttons, and vehicle tires now visibly rotate.
highlights: New dimension "Sky" debuts, reachable through Glowstone portals that rarely generate on the overworld surface
Angel Merchants live in the Sky, each with a randomized selection of trades. You can obtain "Angel Wings" that let you glide, plus dedicated arrows and bows
Added a safety net for falling out of the sky (you land safely above the Overworld)
Added summoning stones for all 10 bosses, craftable so you can summon them anytime. All bosses gained a signature move (triggers below 50% HP, with a 4-second telegraph)
The 3 colossal bosses now have their power rolled randomly on spawn (30-45x the Ender Dragon's HP, then fixed thereafter)
New weapons — "Grim Reaper's Scythe," "Abyssal Trident," and "Thunder Spear" — now drop from their respective bosses
Added a toggle button to the Building Materials mod's crafting bench, letting you pick between multiple blocks from the same layout (like wooden pillar blocks)
The boss-exclusive shovel and hoe can now actually make paths and till soil
Vehicle tires now visibly rotate as you drive (10 vehicle types)
known_limitations: The Sculk Golem and Rock Lock still don't have dedicated attack animations (their signature-move telegraph is particles only)
The Thunder Spear still can't be thrown (melee only)

changelog.title: Fixed a Visual Bug with Worn Angel Gear
changelog.summary: Fixed a bug where actually equipping "Angel Gear" would show vanilla Netherite armor on your body and a plain Elytra on your back. It was an easy bug to miss since the inventory icons displayed correctly.
highlights: Fixed Angel Gear (armor and Angel Wings) to correctly display its dedicated silver-and-gold design when worn

changelog.title: Major Gun Damage Buff & 40 New Doors
changelog.summary: Massively buffed the Laser Gun and Assault Rifle's damage — 20x and 10x respectively. This damage boost significantly throws off the combat balance against existing bosses. Also fixed a bug where the auto turret had actually never fired a single shot, guardrails that wouldn't connect to each other, and lasers that pointed backward when facing east or west. The Building Materials mod also gained 40 new door types (version 1.4.3 was skipped).
highlights: Laser Gun damage buffed 8.0 → 160.0 (20x, 960 DPS), Assault Rifle damage buffed 20.0 → 200.0 (10x, 2,000 DPS)
Fixed a bug where the auto turret had actually never fired a single shot (its aiming ray started from inside its own hitbox). Also reworked target detection so it no longer targets bosses or Wardens
Fixed guardrails not connecting to each other
Fixed lasers pointing backward when facing east or west

Laser trap range 32 → 128 blocks (config cap expanded to 256). It can now be aimed in 26 directions (including diagonals and up/down) — right-click empty-handed to rotate 45° horizontally, sneak+right-click to change the angle
Added 40 new door types to the Building Materials mod (49 total, including the existing 9)
balance_changes: Laser Gun: damage 8.0 → 160.0 (20x)
Assault Rifle: damage 20.0 → 200.0 (10x)
warnings: [Important] This damage buff significantly throws off the combat balance against existing bosses (you can kill them in seconds). No resistance has been added to bosses, so if this bothers you, adjust the damage values in config/sorakaze_guns.json
You need to delete config/sorakaze_guns.json for the gun damage buff to take effect
v1.4.3 was skipped and was never distributed

changelog.title: Fixed the Sky Dimension Crash
changelog.summary: Fixed a serious bug where the client would always crash on entering the Sky dimension (caused by the game having zero renderers registered for drawing Angels and Angel Golems). Also buffed the Heavy Sniper Rifle's damage and added a new scope zoom level.
highlights: [Important] Fixed a bug that always crashed the client on entering the Sky dimension (caused by Angel/Angel Golem rendering never being registered). The same bug also occurred with Angels left over in old worlds from before the Sky relocation
Changed the Heavy Sniper Rifle's damage to 4x the regular Sniper Rifle's (40.0 → 80.0)
Added a new "×12" scope zoom level (Heavy Sniper Rifle only)
Changed it so mouse-wheel input is ignored while looking through a scope (prevents accidentally switching hotbar slots)
balance_changes: Heavy Sniper Rifle: damage 40.0 → 80.0 (4x the regular Sniper Rifle)
known_limitations: Whether this fix actually resolves the Sky dimension crash hasn't been confirmed by actual play yet. Please check whether entering the Sky dimension no longer crashes, and report it if it still does

changelog.title: Sky City Reworked into a Futuristic City, New Boss Arrives

Fixed bugs in the sky-bound city-state of "Singapore" where buildings wouldn't generate at all, the same hotel would keep getting built over and over, and trees or villages would remain floating in midair. [Guns] Added the new weapon "Rocket Launcher" and its dedicated ammo. It deals direct-hit plus explosion damage, and terrain destruction is off by default.
[Building Materials] Doors now close even with someone standing in the doorway. They're designed to have no hitbox while closing, so you won't take damage from being caught in one.

[Building Materials] Added colored Reinforced Glass Panes (17 colors), 5 decorative blocks (smartphone-, laptop-, and desktop-shaped), and a vault door. Also expanded the security camera's max video resolution (the default is unchanged).

changelog.title: Config Auto-Repair (v1.8.0 Reissue)
changelog.summary: A fixed version reissued the same day. In the original v1.8.0, old values left over in earlier versions' config files were overwriting the new defaults, so things like the security camera's resolution, Excalibur's stats, and the Rocket Launcher's terrain destruction weren't taking effect. Going forward, you no longer need to manually delete config files with every update — a new mechanism automatically updates only "stale values set by an earlier version" to the current defaults on startup.
highlights: Introduced a mechanism that automatically detects "fossil" values left over from an earlier version and rewrites them to the current defaults. You no longer need to manually delete config files for future updates.
It never touches values you've tuned yourself — a value only gets updated if it matches a past version's default exactly.

With this fix, the security camera's resolution (768 → 3840), Excalibur's stats (attack power 12 → 75, attack speed 1.8 → 0.6), the Rocket Launcher's terrain destruction, and more now correctly take effect in actual play.
5 mods were updated this time: Boss, Building Materials, Guns, Sky, and Survival. Rail and Vehicles are unchanged this time.
warnings: This reissue ships under the same version number and filenames as the original v1.8.0. If you have the original v1.8.0, discard it and replace it with this version.
From now on, the "please delete your config files" step we used to mention with every update is no longer necessary.
known_limitations: Excalibur's new stats and the Rocket Launcher's terrain destruction effect haven't been confirmed in actual play yet.

changelog.title: Power Mod Added — Redstone Now Needs Electricity
changelog.summary: The 8th mod, "Power," joins the pack. In one of this project's biggest changes yet, vanilla redstone circuitry — redstone dust, repeaters, comparators, redstone blocks, and redstone torches — now needs electricity from a generator to function. Every existing redstone contraption, from auto-farms to stations to automatic doors, will shut down until you wire up a power grid.
highlights: The 8th mod, "Power," joins the pack. You can now build out a power grid with generators, nuclear plants, breaker panels, cables, and more.

17 components — levers, buttons, pressure plates, tripwire hooks, observers, daylight sensors, sculk sensors, targets, trapped chests, detector rails, lecterns, jukeboxes, lightning rods, and more — still work without electricity, as before (manually opening/closing doors and gates works as usual too).

A redstone block will naturally break about 10 minutes after being placed, returning to your inventory as an item (this prevents a "free power source" that needs no electricity from just sitting around).

3 special exceptions — the Void Trash block, laser emitter, and auto turret — are designed the opposite way: without power, they stay "active" as a safety measure (so you don't accidentally lose important items or mobs).
Fixed the Sniper Rifle, Heavy Sniper Rifle, and Laser Gun's projectile speed to the intended value (no change to damage, fire rate, magazine size, durability, or range).
balance_changes: Sniper Rifle / Heavy Sniper Rifle projectile speed: 16.0 → 24.0 (1.5x)
Laser Gun projectile speed: 16.0 → 48.0 (3x)
warnings: Every existing setup that uses redstone circuitry — auto-farms, stations, automatic doors, and so on — will shut down. You'll need to wire up a power grid (generators and cables) from scratch.
To fully revert this change, set powerEnabled to false in config/sorakaze_power.json. To revert redstone specifically while keeping the rest, set redstoneRequiresPower to false in the same file.
Observers and daylight sensors are intentionally left needing no electricity, so you retain an in-game way to recover a base that's lost power.
known_limitations: How it actually feels to play in a world where redstone stops working, and how thoroughly farms and stations end up shut down, are unverified.
The cables lighting up, the breaker panel's screen, and the appearance of the generator and nuclear plant haven't been confirmed on real hardware yet.
After switching power off and back on, an isolated cable not connected to a breaker panel can sometimes stay lit (breaking and replacing it fixes it).

changelog.title: Bigger Air Conditioner & Simplified Power Device Placement
changelog.summary: Significantly enlarged the air conditioner, giving it real presence in a room. Also streamlined the Power mod's devices so each one is complete just by placing a single item, and fixed a bug where the fireplace had zero effect in snowy biomes.
highlights: Enlarged the air conditioner (now roughly 3.1×2.0×2.1 blocks). It's built from an outdoor unit with a round fan, coil fins, and a glowing control panel, plus an indoor unit with 3 louvers jutting outward — making it one of the largest devices in the Power mod.
Unified Power mod devices so you no longer need to assemble multiple blocks — placing a single item now completes the whole thing.
Fixed a bug where the fireplace had zero effect in snowy biomes. Terrain cold and equipment warmth are now calculated separately.
balance_changes: Snowy plains, standing next to your own lit fireplace: felt temperature -24.0°C (frostbite damage) → +2.4°C (safe)
Roofed base, nighttime, snowing, with a fireplace: -18.6°C → +7.9°C
warnings: If you're standing outside in a blizzard at night, a single fireplace can still sometimes not be enough (combine it with a roof, armor, or an additional fireplace).
known_limitations: Whether the temperature balance feels right in actual play hasn't been verified yet.
The new 3D appearance of the 9 auto-sorting blocks is unconfirmed.

changelog.title: Appliances Go Electric, and Machines Generate Heat
changelog.summary: 5 Building Materials devices — the security camera, elevator, escalator, automatic door, and ATM — now require electricity. Also, running machines like generators and nuclear plants now heat up the surrounding room, and without ventilation or cooling, you can start taking heat damage.
highlights: The security camera, elevator, escalator, automatic door, and ATM now require electricity (already-placed ones are affected starting from the next server start too). The elevator still works "going down" even without power, to prevent getting trapped.

Running machines like generators and nuclear plants now heat up their surroundings. Leave 8 machines running uncooled and the room temperature climbs to roughly 77.8°C, with damage starting after about 14 seconds.
Fixed the air conditioner to actually consume power properly (previously it was treated as consuming none).
balance_changes: Machine heat: leaving 8 uncooled machines running raises room temperature to roughly 77.8°C, with heat damage starting after about 14 seconds
warnings: You'll need to wire cables to the security camera, elevator, escalator, automatic door, and ATM. Already-placed equipment will also stop working as of the next server start.
Areas around heat-generating machines like generators become dangerously hot without ventilation or air-conditioner cooling.
known_limitations: How the 5 newly electrified devices (security camera, elevator, escalator, automatic door, ATM) actually behave — with or without power — is unconfirmed.
The appearance and usability of the 3 new generator types and their fuel slots are unconfirmed.

changelog.title: New Weapons, Phone OS, Water Pipes, Seasons & Sky Expansion
changelog.summary: Added a big batch of features at once: 2 new weapons (Handgun and Submachine Gun), a Missile Launcher with 2 warhead types, real OS functionality for phones and computers, water pipes, an elevator that actually moves, and a spring/summer/fall/winter season system. Also raised the Overworld's build height ceiling (no change underground), and drastically reduced the list of sorting blocks and hoppers that required electricity.
highlights: Added 2 new weapons: the Handgun (200/sec, 12-round magazine, semi-auto) and Submachine Gun (450/sec, 40-round magazine, full-auto). Both use the existing small-caliber rounds, so no new ammo type was added.

Added the Missile Launcher (a placed weapon) along with Missile Warheads and Nuclear Warheads (the nuclear warhead has a cap on how many blocks it can destroy; both are Missile-Launcher-only and can't be fired while held).
Added a 2x zoom sight and lock-on feature to the Rocket Launcher (locks on after aiming for 1 second continuously; won't lock onto a target that's running).

Added real OS functionality to phones and computers (7 apps: camera feed, messages, lookup, weather, calculator, phone, and camera). Launch it by holding it and right-clicking, or pressing H — you can even take a photo and send it via message.
Added water pipes (supply water from a river or ocean to a cauldron or farmland). Also added an elevator whose car actually moves up and down.
Added Heavy-gauge Cable (reaches 4x the distance of regular cable), Shielded Cable (8x), and the LED Panel to the Power mod.
Completely reworked ore textures. Added the new material "Lavender Jade" (even rarer than Ruby), the Gas Mask, and the Aero Shield.
Added a season system (8 days per season, 32 days per year). Deserts in summer and snowy plains in winter are now harsher than before.
The Enhanced Beacon's Alpha and Beta tiers (Boss mod) are now craftable. Also, the base Enhanced Beacon no longer needs electricity (reverting the requirement added back in v1.8.1).
Raised the Overworld's build height ceiling from y=319 to y=1023 (no change to underground or the bottom of the world).

Drastically shrank the list of devices requiring electricity from 17 down to 3 (Void Trash block, laser emitter, auto turret). Hoppers, the 8 auto-sorting blocks, the conveyor belt, both traffic light types, and the automatic train stop block now all work without electricity.
balance_changes: Assault Rifle: measured 4,500 → 5,850 damage/sec
Minigun: measured 250 → 50 damage/sec (a heavy nerf — now weaker than a diamond sword)
Sniper Rifle and Heavy Sniper Rifle damage also increased. The durability calculation factor for sniper-class weapons also changed 0.5 → 0.6
warnings: Rockets fired from the Missile Launcher keep destroying terrain even with mobGriefing set to false. To stop only the terrain destruction, set rocketDestroysTerrain to false in the config.
The Overworld's build height was extended to y=1023. This affects everyone, even if you never use the Sky dimension (no change underground).

Since the list of sorting blocks and hoppers requiring power was drastically shrunk, devices that had previously been stopped will automatically start working again. Watch out for unexpected reactivation in areas you haven't touched in a while.
The gun damage changes above are applied automatically. No config deletion or editing is needed, but you can revert them individually by specifying values in the config.
known_limitations: Immediately after release, the Enhanced Beacon Alpha/Beta had a bug preventing ability selection (fixed in the next update).
Immediately after release, the Missile Launcher didn't show up in the creative tab and had no display name set. Icons for both warhead types were also missing (resolved in the next update).
The phone/computer apps didn't have dedicated icon art yet — just a row of colored squares (improved in the next update).

changelog.title: Fixed Water Pipe, Enhanced Beacon & Gas Mask Bugs
changelog.summary: Fixed several bugs reported after v1.8.4: water pipes being unbreakable, the Enhanced Beacon Alpha/Beta not letting you pick abilities, and the gas mask appearing to float above the head. Also fixed the hostile mob spawn cap to correctly apply to the Overworld only, and changed the default to a flat 150 mobs.
highlights: Fixed water pipes being unbreakable. A unit mix-up meant the hitbox was only 1/32nd the visual thickness (hardness and tool requirements themselves were correct from the start).
Also fixed water pipe intakes standing alone in a river getting swept away and disappearing (redesigned as a waterlogging-capable block).

Fixed the Enhanced Beacon Alpha/Beta not letting you pick abilities. The screen would auto-close the very next tick after opening, and selections weren't being saved either (the standard Enhanced Beacon was unaffected).
Fixed the gas mask appearing to float above the head. Created a new dedicated 3D model and repositioned it to fit the face.

Reverted the Firework Doll's appearance from the 3D "plush toy" look added in v1.8.4 back to the flat art style it had through v1.8.3 (per the owner's request). No changes to functionality like the use-count limit.

Changed the Overworld hostile mob spawn cap from the previous "15x vanilla" (roughly 1,050 mobs) to a flat 150 mobs. Doesn't affect the Nether, the End, or the Sky (also fixed the earlier bug where this mistakenly applied to every dimension).
warnings: No config deletion or editing needed. The spawn cap value updates to the new default automatically.
known_limitations: The new appearance of the water pipe and gas mask, and how the Enhanced Beacon GUI feels to use, haven't been confirmed in actual play yet.
Whether the new spawn density of 150 mobs feels right in actual play hasn't been verified yet.

changelog.title: Added Missile Warhead & Phone App Icons
changelog.summary: Two fixes related to appearance and discoverability. Resolved the missile and nuclear warheads having zero textures by drawing dedicated icons from scratch and making them craftable. Also added the Missile Launcher, which players reported being unable to find, to the creative tab, and filled in the translations for its display name and control panel. The phone/computer's 7 apps also got dedicated new icons.
highlights: Drew dedicated 128px icons for the missile and nuclear warheads from scratch (previously there was no art at all — they showed up in your inventory as Minecraft's standard "purple-and-black checkerboard" missing-texture pattern).
Made the missile warhead (5 Iron Ingots + 1 TNT + 1 Redstone Block) and nuclear warhead (4 Blocks of Iron + 4 TNT + 1 Nether Star) craftable for the first time.

Added the Missile Launcher to the creative tab (crafting it was already possible before, but it never appeared in the tab, so it couldn't be found). Also added the display name and translations for its control panel screen — target coordinate entry, 9 status displays, 8 compass directions, the safety switch, and more (54 strings each in Japanese and English).

Drew dedicated new icons for all 7 phone/computer apps (camera feed, messages, lookup, weather, calculator, phone, camera) — previously it was just a row of colored squares. Also added per-app flourishes, like a precipitation icon and enlarged clock in the weather app, a recessed LCD-style design in the calculator app, a compass-needle display in the phone app, and a surveillance-monitor look for the camera feed app.
Improved it so opening an app now always shows that app's icon and name at the top of the screen.
warnings: Making the missile and nuclear warheads craftable was a decision made by the dev team (not an explicit request from the owner). If the balance feels too strong or excessive, please talk to the admins.
No config deletion or editing needed this time either.
known_limitations: The "Lookup" app's 3×3 recipe screen can't receive grid-placement data for ingredients from the server, so it falls back to a simplified display that packs ingredients in order from the top-left (the ingredient types and quantities themselves are correct).
The warheads' new icons, the control panel's translations, and the phone app's new screens are all still unconfirmed on the actual in-game screen.
16 of the 17 Reinforced Glass Pane colors still don't have names set, a carryover issue from earlier versions.

changelog.title: Rocket Launcher & Nuclear Warhead Buffed, Gun Sound Effects Overhauled
changelog.summary: Raised the Rocket Launcher's power 8x and significantly widened the Nuclear Warhead's blast radius. Also gave the scope and lock-on — which were already working correctly but easy to miss — new sound effects that make them much easier to notice. The Nuclear Warhead can now also be used as the Power mod's new top-tier fuel.
highlights: Rocket Launcher damage increased 40 → 320 (8x).
Nuclear Warhead direct-hit damage buffed to 320 × 70 = 22,400. Its blast radius was also significantly widened, but it's designed to be safe — it won't destroy bedrock or unloaded terrain.

Created new sound effects for while you're aiming down the scope and for the instant a lock-on completes. Previously these used vanilla's generic UI sound, so even though the features themselves worked fine, they were easy to miss.
The Nuclear Warhead can now be used as fuel for the Power mod — an energy source with roughly 100x the output and 144x the burn time (about 1 hour) of a vanilla bucket of lava.
balance_changes: Rocket Launcher power: 40 → 320 (8x)
Nuclear Warhead direct-hit damage: 22,400 (320 × 70)
warnings: No config deletion needed. The defaults update automatically.

The Missile Launcher itself still has no way to protect against its own explosion. Its minimum range (24 blocks) is smaller than the Nuclear Warhead's blast radius (64 blocks), so aiming at a nearby target can destroy the launcher along with it.
known_limitations: The look of the nuclear explosion (particles, screen shake) and the new sound effects haven't been confirmed in actual play yet.
FPS and lag during a large-scale nuclear explosion with players present haven't been verified.

changelog.title: Nuclear Warhead Buffed Again, Battery Added to the Power Mod
changelog.summary: Buffed the Nuclear Warhead's direct-hit damage another 3x, and its impact sound now carries much farther. The Power mod also gained a new block, the Battery, changing how generator power gets delivered.
highlights: Nuclear Warhead direct-hit damage increased 22,400 → 67,200 (3x).
The impact sound now carries out to a 20,000-block radius. The launch sound is also much louder now.
The Missile Launcher was made larger, and a staged, spreading destruction effect plus a flash were added for Nuclear Warhead impacts.

Added a new block, the Battery, to the Power mod. Power from generators and nuclear plants is now first stored in a Battery, which produces Energy Cells once it's charged up. You take the resulting Energy Cells and plug them into a Breaker Panel's fuel slot to use them.
balance_changes: Nuclear Warhead direct-hit damage: 22,400 → 67,200 (3x)
warnings: [Important] Generators and nuclear plants can no longer deliver power to a Breaker Panel without going through a Battery. Wiring them the old way — "generator → cable → breaker panel" — by itself no longer delivers electricity. Solar Panels, Wind Turbines, and Water Flow Generators still deliver power directly, as before.
No config deletion needed.
known_limitations: 2 of the Nuclear Warhead-related tests couldn't be fully confirmed when run under heavy load in the dev environment (the warhead's detonation and destruction themselves have been confirmed working via live detonation tests on a real server).
The look of the Battery's lid open/close animation hasn't been confirmed.

changelog.title: New Mod "Backrooms" Joins the Pack, Wither Storm Overhauled
changelog.summary: The 9th mod, "Backrooms," has joined the pack — a sanity-driven exploration experience reached through rifts that spawn near End Cities. The boss mod's Wither Storm has been completely overhauled with a new look, growth stages, and a new status effect, plus new guaranteed drops. The other 6 mods (building & decor, guns, power, sky, rail, vehicles) are unchanged.
highlights: The 9th mod, "Backrooms" (sorakaze_backrooms), has joined the pack. Every time an End City generates, exactly one rift (an altar) spawns nearby in a safe spot — one per City (existing End Cities don't get one).

Features a sanity system. It maxes out at 100 and drains to zero in about 18 minutes if you do nothing. Drinking the restorative item found in chests recovers 35. Roughly every 30 seconds there's a 12% chance of a "blackout," and things start to change once sanity drops below 20.
You can't place blocks inside the maze, and the walls, floor, and ceiling — including the chests — can't be destroyed at all. Other dimensions are unaffected.
The entity "Hollow Listener" roams the maze (40 HP, 6 attack damage. It freezes while you're looking at it and moves again once you look away). Up to 3 can be present at once.
A 3-stage progress tracker (① confirm you're alive → ② gather traces → ③ escape) stays on screen at all times.

Completely remade the Wither Storm boss's appearance. Replaced the old fixed-HP, single-stage design with a growth-stage system (S0 Embryo → S1 Gorging → S2 Hunting → S3 Rampage → S4 Tempest → S5 Zenith, HP ranging 600–24,000). It advances stages based on how many items and mobs it has absorbed, and from S2 onward it floats and generates a gravity field that pulls things toward it.

Added a new status effect, "Wither Sickness." It sets in after repeated exposure to the tractor beam or gravity field (the default is half of vanilla Wither's damage-per-second; drinking milk cures it like any other status effect).
Added an admin command, /glimpse storm restore [radius], which restores terrain the Wither Storm has devoured by writing it back from a log.

Added 2 new guaranteed drops for the Wither Storm: "Omnigatherer α" (32 durability, same as a golden pickaxe, and not enchantable — a separate item from the existing plain "Omnigatherer") and "Firework Doll α" (unlimited uses, but with a 3-minute cooldown between uses — an upgraded version of the existing Firework Doll).
Discontinued bundling the recipe reference sheet (レシピ早見表.html) with releases. Crafting reference has moved to this site.
warnings: We did not implement the name "Almond Water" that the owner had requested, since it's judged to be a proper name tied specifically to the sanity-restoring item within Backrooms creative communities. The function (restores sanity, found in chests, single-use) is unchanged — only the name was reworked, to "Drop of Calm."
If you right-click a chest while holding a block item, the block-placement restriction triggers first and the chest won't open. Empty your hand or switch to a different item before opening it.
No config deletion or edits are needed. This update only adds new settings — none of the existing settings' defaults have changed.
known_limitations: The overall look of Backrooms (the maze wallpaper and lighting mood, the entity's appearance and freeze effect, the blackout effect, the progress-tracker HUD display, and the contents of chests) has not yet been confirmed in actual gameplay.
The Wither Storm's new appearance, how its form changes at each growth stage, the gravity field's visual effect, and the look of it devouring terrain are also unconfirmed.
The visual/audio effect of contracting Wither Sickness, and the appearance (icon and in-hand model) of Omnigatherer α and Firework Doll α, are also unconfirmed.
Backrooms's dedicated boot-proof task (runBackroomsBoot) hasn't yet been run as a standalone check on a dedicated server (the 9-mod simultaneous boot test did confirm the dimension loads).
Sync between two simultaneous players, and server load with all 9 mods running at once, are untested.
The attack animations for the Sculk Golem, Rock Lock, Kraken, and Titan, and the ability to throw the Lightning Spear, are once again carried over to a future update.

changelog.title: Fixed End City Rifts and Wither Storm Flight, Added a Video App
changelog.summary: Fixed a bug where the Backrooms rifts added in v1.9.0 were effectively never generating, and a bug where the Wither Storm's airborne-stage flight had never actually been implemented. The building & decor mod gained a "Video" app for phones and computers, along with device-specific OS-style screens, and Survival's Spark Doll α now has its finalized appearance.
highlights: Backrooms: Fixed a bug where End City rifts were, in measured practice, essentially never generating. The check was looking at the height (Y coordinate), but the coordinate it actually received always had a height of 0, so it was always misjudged as "absent." On newly generated land, every End City is now guaranteed exactly one rift (this doesn't retroactively apply to existing land). Also redrew the icon art for the Drop of Calm, Flashlight, and Torn Note.

Wither Storm: Implemented genuine 3D flight for the airborne stages (S3–S5) — circling in, diving to attack, then peeling away. The grounded stages (S0–S2), melee attack, head barrage, tractor beam, and Great Vortex damage formulas are unchanged.

Building & decor: Added a "Video" app to phones and computers (it embeds an actual browser engine; the first time a player opens it, a one-time extra download runs on their PC). Screens now vary by device model — iPhone gets an iOS-style look, while MacBook and Mac Studio get a Macintosh-style look (menu bar, Dock).
Survival: Finalized Spark Doll α's appearance (a visual-only change; functionality is unchanged).
warnings: This release listed the Video app's first-time download size as "roughly 140–175MB," but that was the compressed size and was incorrect (corrected to a measured ~300MB in v1.9.0.3).
No config deletion or editing needed. This update only adds new settings.
known_limitations: At this point, the Backrooms rifts themselves were fixed, but a separate bug remained where the maze beyond them wasn't generating at all (discovered and fixed in v1.9.0.2).
Whether the Video app actually displays web pages, and how the new iPhone/macOS-style screen designs look, were both still unconfirmed.
Whether the Wither Storm's airborne-stage flight actually looks natural in motion (the feel of the circling and diving) was also unconfirmed.

changelog.title: Fixed Backrooms Maze Not Generating (World Action Required)
changelog.summary: v1.9.0.1 fixed the rifts themselves, but we discovered — and fixed — a bug where the Backrooms dimension beyond them stayed completely empty (the void). If your world has ever had a player visit Backrooms, you'll need to delete the dimension folder. Also fixed the appearance bug affecting 3 items, and Survival's Spark Doll α has been replaced with artwork drawn by the owner themselves.
highlights: Backrooms: Fixed a bug where passing through a rift led nowhere — there was no maze anywhere, and even in Creative you'd die instantly. The cause was tripping both of two filters in Minecraft's "superflat" world-generation system, so the maze had never actually been built in any chunk. Also placed bedrock beneath the floor and added a rescue procedure in case you do fall through.

Backrooms: Fixed a bug where the Drop of Calm, Flashlight, and Torn Note all showed up in your inventory as the "purple-and-black checkerboard" missing-texture pattern. The definition file that determines their art was missing entirely.
Survival: Replaced Spark Doll α's art with pixel art drawn by the owner themselves. No functional changes (mechanics, recipe, drops, or config).
warnings: [Important] If your world has ever had a player visit Backrooms, stop the server and delete the <world name>/dimensions/sorakaze_backrooms/backrooms/ folder. The next time someone passes through a rift, it will be rebuilt as a proper new maze. Backrooms is a dimension where you can't place or break blocks, so deleting it costs you nothing (items like the Drop of Calm, Flashlight, and Torn Note in your inventory won't disappear). If you can't find the folder, no one has entered that world yet, so there's nothing you need to do.
No config deletion or editing needed (just 2 new settings added, which take effect automatically).
known_limitations: How the fixed maze actually looks (the mood of the yellow wallpaper, etc.), the art for the 3 fixed items, and how Spark Doll α's new art looks were all still unconfirmed on an actual screen at this point.

changelog.title: Completely Redesigned the Phone/Computer "Mine OS" Screens, Fixed Icon Bug
changelog.summary: This update touches only the building & decor mod. Completely remade the look of the phone/computer "Mine OS" screens and added 3 new apps: Settings, Terminal, and Music. Also fixed the app icon bug that had persisted since v1.8.6. Additionally, we've corrected the Video app's first-time download size and discovered it doesn't work on macOS.
highlights: Completely redesigned the phone/computer screens, adding frosted-glass-style translucent panels, rounded corners, and shadows. Computers now have 3 traffic-light buttons in the top-left, a "Mine OS ▸ App Name" breadcrumb up top, and a Dock at the bottom; phones gained a status bar, home indicator, and lock screen. The Messages app now shows chat-style speech bubbles with the other person's head icon.

Added 3 new apps (8 → 11 total): Settings (device/server info and a sound toggle), Terminal (help, about, ping, tps, and cls respond instantly; anything else is sent as a chat command), and Music (plays songs from music discs available on this server).

Fixed a bug, present since v1.8.6, where app icons were hidden behind a gray panel. The cause was vanilla's opaque button background getting drawn over the same spot right after the icon was rendered (the artwork itself had been correct from the start).

Fixed text overflowing or getting cut off on screen, and added a new automated check to keep it from happening again (measured 4,773 locations across 2 languages × 23 screen sizes, confirming zero overflows).
warnings: ⚠ The Video app does not work on macOS Minecraft (confirmed by testing; Windows and Linux remain supported). Starting with this release, macOS no longer silently freezes — it now shows "Not available on this OS" and stops.
[Correction] The Video app's first-time download is not "roughly 140–175MB" — measured, it's about 300MB (correcting the inaccurate figure given as of v1.9.0.1).
No config deletion or editing needed (just 4 new settings added, all defaulting to "shown").
known_limitations: Mine OS's new look, the feel of using the 3 new apps (Settings, Terminal, Music), and whether the Music app actually plays sound were all still unconfirmed on an actual screen at this point.
Whether the icon bug was actually resolved hadn't been visually confirmed — the fix was based only on analysis of the draw order.
Whether the Video app actually displays web pages on real Windows/Linux machines remained unconfirmed.

changelog.title: Verified Nuclear-Warhead Power Generation, Major Rail Update, New Screen Design, Always-On Coordinates
changelog.summary: Updated 5 mods at once (there are no v1.9.1 or v1.9.2 releases — the major rail update and the nuclear-warhead power generation requests are bundled together and shipped as v1.9.3). We've finally delivered Spark Doll α's art, which had actually been fixed two releases ago but had never once made it into a shipped build, along with a fix for batteries breaking when left fully charged for a long time, a new (not-yet-run) way to verify on a real server that nuclear warheads can be used as fuel, and a fix for the Rocket Launcher's scope bug. Rail gained a major update including automatic departure and automatic driving, Power/Guns/Boss screens got the new "Glimpse Glass" design, and always-on coordinate and TPS/ping displays were added.
highlights: [Important] The Spark Doll α art bug (part of the right ear appearing to vanish) had actually already been fixed after v1.9.0.2, but a flaw in the mechanism that compares build outputs meant it never once made it into a distributed build. The fixed art finally arrives with this release. To make sure this never happens again, we've introduced a new check (check_dist_drift.py) that directly diffs source assets against the distributed build.

[Important] Power: Fixed a bug where a fully charged Battery, left alone for about 18.6 hours, would stop producing Energy Cells forever. The cause was an addition overflow, which showed up faster with higher-output fuels (like nuclear warheads). Batteries already broken by this bug will fix themselves automatically once you install this release.

Power: The mechanism for using nuclear warheads as fuel has existed since v1.8.7, but this round we set up a way to verify it on a real dedicated server for the first time (however, the test environment was lost during this packaging round, so it hasn't actually been run yet -- see the warning below for details). Also fixed a bug where the fuel-grade display showed the raw, untranslated string "sorakaze_power.fuel_quality.nuclear."

Guns: The Rocket Launcher's scope is finally visible on screen (fixed after being reported twice). Its zoom level has also been raised from ×2 to ×4. The appearance of both sniper rifles is unchanged.

Major Rail update: added automatic departure, automatic driving, running sound, overhead catenary wires (decorative only), interior cabin lights and headlights, arrival announcement displays, the ability to walk around inside the train, and the ability to sit in seats. The speedometer moved to the top of the screen and is no longer shown to passengers — only the driver sees it.

Adopted a new translucent design, "Glimpse Glass," for Power/Guns/Boss screens (Battery, Breaker Panel, Missile Launcher, Enhanced Beacon, and more). Also added background blur for when you open your inventory or a chest. A new optional resource pack, Glimpse_Alpha_Glass_UI_Pack.zip, is now bundled as well, which extends the glass look to vanilla screens too.

Coordinates (including facing direction) are now always shown on screen. The TPS/ping display was also redesigned, and the default changed from "only while holding Tab" to "always shown" (you can restore the old behavior via config).
balance_changes: Rocket Launcher scope zoom: ×2 → ×4
warnings: Within the major Rail update, adding higher-tier train cars and coupling with vanilla minecarts were both deferred this time (only a design document was produced). Coupling with vanilla minecarts touches on this project's policy of "never replacing or removing vanilla elements," so it will be decided separately after further discussion.

Proof of the dedicated-server verification for using nuclear warheads as fuel could not actually be carried out this time, since the test environment was lost during the packaging process (the mechanism itself for using nuclear warheads as fuel is unchanged since v1.8.7).
If you still haven't deleted the Backrooms world folder as described in the v1.9.0.2 change, please make sure to take care of that as well.
No config deletion or editing needed. Everything added this time is a brand-new setting.
known_limitations: Nearly all of the new Rail features (automatic departure, automatic driving, running sound, catenary wires, cabin lights, arrival announcements, walking around inside the train) were still unconfirmed on real hardware at this point.
The look of the new "Glimpse Glass" screen design and the look of the new resource pack were both also unconfirmed.
The actual on-screen look of the always-on coordinate and TPS/ping displays was also unconfirmed.
3 automated tests in Guns and 1 in Power remain flaky, with results varying from run to run. All of them have been confirmed to concern existing code that wasn't changed in this release.

changelog.title: The V2 update — a 10th mod, Planarcadia; four new bosses; plumbing, gasoline and food spoilage
changelog.summary: This is V2 proper. The 10th mod, Planarcadia, shipped here for the first time. The Boss mod gained four new bosses, each with its own summoning ritual; Survival gained water infrastructure and a refrigerator; Vehicles gained gasoline; Power gained an air purifier. The Backrooms grew a great deal, and Building & Decor gained blackout reinforced glass in every colour.
highlights: A 10th mod, Planarcadia (sorakaze_planarcadia), is bundled for the first time. Build a frame out of Portal Amethyst Blocks in the same shape as a Nether portal, light it, and it opens onto a pleasure world where night rules. It brings its own blocks — LED signs, the phantom moon, the Interplanar Jump Mural, a shop counter. It does not depend on any other Glimpse Alpha mod.

Four new bosses joined the Boss mod: the Volcanic Golem King (Forge Altar Core + Molten Crown), the Abyssal Kraken Warden (Sculk Heart + Sonar Eye), the Prismatic Ice Phoenix Dragon (Frost Altar + Primal Egg), and the Witherstorm Demon Overlord (Soul Blood Altar + 3 wither skeleton skulls + a nether star).

The Soul Blood Altar refuses the Witherstorm Demon Overlord until all three of the others have been killed. Each of the four has a guaranteed drop: the Volcanic Core, the Abyssal Sinew, the Prismatic Plume and the Overlord's Heart.
The Gravebound Reaper now has a small chance of dropping the Soul-Reaping Scythe. Anything you kill with that scythe has a small chance of dropping its own spawn egg.
Survival gained water infrastructure: pipes, a pump and a tap. The pump draws, the pipes carry, the tap fills. A refrigerator and Spoiled Food arrived with it.
Vehicles gained gasoline. Right-click a vehicle while holding a Gasoline Canister to refuel it. The empty canister does not break — refill it at a crafting table with 4 coal or charcoal.

Power gained an Air Purifier. Running a nuclear plant now pollutes the air around it, and standing in polluted air gives you slowness, then weakness, then poison. A powered purifier clears that pollution locally for as long as it has electricity.

Guns gained a data-driven firearm and attachment system. Put a gun and its attachments into the Gun Workbench and they are fitted the moment you take the gun back out; put a fitted gun back in and they come off. Three guns (Service Pistol, Marksman Carbine, Breaching Shotgun) and six attachments (Red Dot Sight, Suppressor, Extended Magazine, Angled Foregrip, Heavy Stock, Laser Pointer) use it. A Hazmat Suit that blocks nuclear contamination was also added — you need it and the gas mask together.

The Backrooms grew a great deal: Levels 0, 1 and 2, the Poolrooms, the party level and a hub hall lined with numbered doors, plus twelve entities (Hound, Smiler, Faceling, Skin Stealer, Peeling Colossus, Wailing Hulk, Pallid Runner, Partygoer, Deathmoth, Duller, Living Painting, False Puddle) and things to carry — almond water, bandages, a flashlight, a blood test kit, a crowbar, matches.

Building & Decor gained blackout reinforced glass: three shapes (block, pane, plate) in 17 colours. At the same time, the 16 reinforced glass panes that had shipped without a name since v1.7.7 finally got Japanese and English names.
warnings: Version numbers moved from 1.x to 2.0.0 across the board. Replace all ten jars on the server and on every player's PC together.
known_limitations: No V2.0.0 entry was published on this site at the time. This one was written afterwards, alongside the V2.1.0 release, by reading what the shipped jars actually contain.

changelog.title: Backrooms Levels 3–8 become real, endless levels; a server-admin app on the in-game PC; boss summon recipes reach the recipe book
changelog.summary: The largest change this round is Backrooms Levels 3 through 8. They used to be 128-block demo islands; they are now endless levels you can actually walk into and explore. The in-game PC in the Building & Decor mod gained a server-administration app, and in the Boss mod the summoning items' recipes now appear in the in-game recipe book. The three data-driven guns each have their own in-hand model at last.
highlights: Only four mods actually changed: Backrooms, Building & Decor, Boss and Guns. The other six (Planarcadia, Power, Rail, Sky, Survival, Vehicles) were bumped to 2.1.0 only to keep the set consistent — their jars differ from the 2.0.0 ones in exactly one entry, the version string in fabric.mod.json. Not a byte of their content changed.
Backrooms Levels 3 to 8 went from 128-block demo islands to real, endless levels. None of them has an edge any more; all of them can be walked and explored.
Level 3, the Electrical Station. The current is live and touching a panel is dangerous. A Hound patrols, and a Smiler waits in the underground cable room.
Level 4, the Empty Offices. Rated safe — but 3% of the windows are watching you, and they look exactly like the rest. Sanity slowly recovers here. The almond water is in the break room.
Level 5, the Terror Hotel. 80% of the numbered doors are locked. In each contiguous region exactly one room differs in its details. Do not linger.

Level 6, Lights Out. A flashlight works properly for 20 seconds; past that it only works about 15% of any given second. While it is lit, entities notice you from four times as far — light attracts. This is a level you navigate by ear.
Level 7, Thalassophobia. One house of fixed shape, and an ocean with no far shore. Do not walk to the end of the pier.
Level 8, the Cave System. Tunnels dug for people and then abandoned; the iron rails really do lead somewhere. There is a flooded winze 32 blocks deep.

The in-game PC gained a "Server Admin" app. Without opening a config file, an administrator can change: whether phone messaging, calls and the browser are allowed; how many camera feeds can be shown at once and whether live feeds are allowed; whether automatic backups run, how often, and how many are kept; and a set of boss knobs (Plague Doctor natural spawn and its chance, thunderstorm-only spawning, respawn cooldown, Plague Wither pack size, wardens required for the Sculk Golem, the Reaper's wither summon count, whether Rock Lock spawners generate in nether fortresses, Plague Doctor max health, Plague Wither health multiplier).

Opening the admin app needs an admin ID and a password. The server administrator hands those out individually, only to the people they choose. They are not written anywhere on this site. Sign-in expires after a while, and failed attempts are rate-limited.

The recipes for the Boss mod's summoning items (Forge Altar Core, Molten Crown, Sculk Heart, Sonar Eye, Frost Altar, Primal Egg, Soul Blood Altar) now appear in the in-game recipe book. Until now they had no unlock path at all, so there was no way to discover how to make them from inside the game.
Four discovery advancements were added as a hint toward summoning: The Scorching Key, The Fathom Key, The Frost Key and The Altar Is Built. Each fires when you hold the matching summoning item.
The Plague Doctor's natural spawn is available again, behind an administrator toggle — but it defaults to OFF. Until an administrator explicitly turns it on, behaviour is identical to V2.0.0.

The three data-driven guns (Service Pistol, Marksman Carbine, Breaching Shotgun) each have their own in-hand model now. All three had been borrowing the assault rifle's mesh, so holding a pistol showed you a rifle.
warnings: Levels 3 to 8 generate in a fundamentally different way now. In a world where you visited the demo islands under V2.0.0, the terrain in that area will not match what was there before.
The admin ID and password for the Server Admin app are never published on this site. Get them from the server administrator directly.
known_limitations: The Sapporo mod (sorakaze_sapporo) is not part of this round. It is deferred to V2.2.
The actual look, sound and entity behaviour of Levels 3–8 had not been confirmed in a real play-through at the time of writing.

changelog.title: 52 new glass lanterns, a real Backrooms lobby, overworld raids, turrets, and a real reconstruction of Sapporo
changelog.summary: This round adds an 11th mod, Sapporo — a dimension recreating the real city of Sapporo, Japan, from real survey data. Backrooms Level 1, "The Lobby", is now a real explorable space rather than a demo room, with a glass objective panel shown on the left of the screen at all times. Village raids can now trigger on pure chance without Bad Omen, turrets let you mount guns and bows, video now plays up to 4K and stops automatically when you walk away, the Sparxie staff gained a ranged attack alongside its melee one, the minigun and rocket launcher were rebalanced, a flyable camera drone and its own phone app arrived, and the Building & Decor mod gained 52 new glass lanterns. The Amethyst Gate now opens with plain vanilla amethyst blocks too.
highlights: The Sapporo mod (sorakaze_sapporo) has finally shipped. It's a dimension recreating the real city of Sapporo, Japan, from real geographic data. Building footprints and terrain are both 100% real survey data, but most building heights are currently a documented per-district statistical estimate — an honest gap while the more detailed 3D building dataset (Japan's PLATEAU) is still being obtained. Heights will be refined once that data is in hand.
Backrooms Level 1, "The Lobby", is now a real, walkable, explorable space rather than a small demo room. You reach it through a rift that generates naturally near an End City.
A glass objective panel is now shown on the left side of the screen at all times, showing your current level, sanity, and where to head next.

Inside the Backrooms, sanity now replaces thirst as the stat you're managing. Entities you meet there take no damage from ordinary weapons and cannot be defeated — this is a place for evasion, not combat.
The Amethyst Gate can now be built from plain vanilla amethyst blocks as well as Portal Amethyst Blocks — the two can even be mixed in the same frame.
Village raids can now start on pure chance just from being in a village, with no need for Bad Omen. 12 waves in total, with extra enemies from the Heaven mod on the final wave.
New turrets let you mount a gun, bow, or crossbow. A mounted weapon carries its own ammo store, and unmounting hands the weapon and remaining ammo back to you.
Video playback now supports up to 4K, always keeps a 16:9 aspect ratio, and stops automatically once you walk far enough away from the screen.
The Sparxie staff can now attack at range (a 24-block bolt) as well as in melee.
The minigun now hits roughly three times as hard, and the rocket launcher's blast is far more powerful than before.

A freely flyable camera drone was added, along with a dedicated Drone App on the in-game phone showing a live 16:9 feed from its point of view. Letting go leaves it hovering in place rather than auto-returning.
The Building & Decor mod gained 52 new glass lanterns (18 vanilla-glass, 17 reinforced, 17 blackout). Full light level 15, and measured brighter than the existing LED panel.
The admin app's PC screen gained a change-log view for the server administrator — a read-only view of past changes. Viewing it is not itself logged.
balance_changes: Minigun damage roughly tripled.
Rocket launcher blast power greatly increased.
warnings: Playing in the Sapporo dimension requires the server administrator to have installed a separate map data file on the server (not distributed on this site). Without it, that world simply isn't reachable.
Backrooms entities cannot be defeated. Don't try to fight them with ordinary weapons — evade instead.
known_limitations: Most Sapporo building heights are still a district-level statistical estimate rather than real survey data. They'll be updated once more detailed 3D city data becomes available.
Whether players can build and light their own Heaven gate (glowstone portal) depends on a server-administrator setting, which defaults to off.

changelog.title: Glass lanterns now genuinely glow in colour, and the Backrooms Level 1 crate mission is fixed
changelog.summary: A player-reported fix release. Glass lanterns had a washed-out, near-white glow that barely showed their colour; they now read as translucent coloured glass genuinely glowing in their own hue, like neon. The Backrooms Level 1 "open 4 crates" objective, which could never be completed, has also been fixed.
highlights: Fixed glass lanterns' appearance: previously the colour was almost entirely washed out by a large white-hot core, so every lantern looked much the same near-white regardless of colour. Now the coloured glow dominates the block, neon-style — red lanterns glow red, blue glow blue, and so on — with only a small white-hot filament left at the very centre. As proper glass, you can still see through it.

Fixed the Backrooms Level 1 "open 4 crates" objective, which never progressed no matter how many crates you opened. Prying a crate open (with a crowbar, or crouch + bare hands) now correctly advances the objective.

changelog.title: Glass lanterns properly fixed, sanity no longer shares the screen with thirst, turret weapons are visible, and Glimpse Launcher arrives
changelog.summary: The V2.2.1 glass lantern fix turned out not to be enough — a player sent a real screenshot showing the lanterns still reading as washed-out and near-white. We've redesigned them properly this time, removing the leftover white-hot centre entirely in favour of a single smooth colour gradient. In the Backrooms, the ordinary thirst bar was still showing up alongside sanity; it's now correctly hidden there. Weapons mounted on turrets were invisible even though they worked correctly; they now render. Several admin settings commands that were documented but didn't actually do anything have been wired up properly. And we're releasing a new desktop app, Glimpse Launcher, that checks for and applies pack updates automatically.
highlights: Redesigned the glass lantern glow again. V2.2.1's fix kept a small white-hot "filament" at the centre of each lantern, but in real play that filament still read as washed-out white regardless of colour — confirmed with a real in-game screenshot. The filament concept has been removed entirely in favour of a single smooth gradient from the centre to the edge. Still genuinely translucent glass.
Fixed the ordinary thirst bar showing up alongside sanity while inside the Backrooms. It's now correctly hidden there (the feature itself is unaffected everywhere else).
Fixed weapons mounted on turrets being invisible. Turrets have always accepted, fired, and returned mounted weapons correctly — they just never rendered. They now do.

Fixed several server admin settings commands that were documented but had no effect (village raid chance and wave count, video resolution cap, and others). The Backrooms module also gained its own admin settings entry point, which it previously had none of.

Released Glimpse Launcher, a new desktop app that checks the Wiki for pack updates, verifies downloads by SHA-256, takes an automatic backup before applying an update, and can open the official Minecraft Launcher for you (you still choose the Fabric profile yourself, exactly as before). One file runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux (Java is required to run it). Get it from the Download page.
known_limitations: This is Glimpse Launcher's first release. The launcher cannot yet update itself automatically — that's planned for a future version.

changelog.title: Fixed a client crash when deploying a drone, and the Server Admin app's sign-in screen
changelog.summary: A player-reported fix release. Deploying a drone previously crashed the client every time; it now works and renders a small quadcopter model. The Server Admin app's sign-in screen also no longer clears the ID field after every failed login attempt.
highlights: Fixed a client crash that happened every time a drone was deployed. Drones now render a small quadcopter model instead of crashing the client.
Fixed the Server Admin app's sign-in screen resetting the ID field to empty after every failed login attempt, which made retyping it necessary each time.
